name: 41118-penaltydecode-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: dense decoder (Qwen3ForCausalLM), 36 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, intermediate 12288, vocab 151936, bf16, max_position_embeddings 40960. 8.19B params = 16.38 GB = 15.26 GiB. KV per token = 2*36*8*128*2 B = 147456 B = 144 KiB. Read off the cached config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=64, warmup the first 50% by completion, bounded at 256 requests with a 3600 s safety cap. 64 is chosen so the whole declared batch is resident to the last token under this card's KV budget -- 64 * 4352 = 278528 tokens = 38.2 GiB against roughly 50 GiB available, argued line by line in vllm-config.yaml -- and it is deliberately EQUAL TO `max-num-seqs`, so the declared streams are exactly the ceiling on what one decode step may hold. 256 requests at 64 streams is four clean waves. THE WARMUP FRACTION IS SIZED AGAINST THE STREAM COUNT, NOT PICKED FOR ROUNDNESS: in a closed loop request k cannot start until request k-64 has finished, and the window opens at the START of request W+1, so a warmup of W excludes about W-64 requests and NOT W. Anything at or below 64 therefore excludes nothing at all. 0.5 * 256 = 128 = twice the stream count, which opens the window one full request-time after the first wave drained and so discards exactly that wave, leaving 192 measured over three waves. THE OPERATING POINT IS SATURATION WITHOUT PREEMPTION AND THAT IS A DECLARATION: if a cliff search walks the stream count it walks it DOWNWARD, because a run above ~64 no longer keeps every stream resident and has left the setup rather than operated it. The workload, the bound and the sampling parameters do not move.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, `request_format: plain`. Prompt EXACTLY 256 tokens (min = max = 256), output EXACTLY 4096 (min = max = 4096). The shape is decode-dominated by construction: 1 prefill step against 4095 decode steps per request, i.e. 99.98% of each request's steps are decode. The backend forces `ignore_eos=True` whenever max_tokens is set, so every request generates exactly 4096 tokens and every request has an identical shape. Context grows from 256 to 4352 tokens within a request. Sampling is what an ordinary chat client sends when it wants varied, non-repetitive text: `temperature: 1.0` and `frequency_penalty: 0.2` in `spec.backend.sampling_params`, both plain OpenAI sampling fields that the in-process backend passes straight into vLLM's SamplingParams. `request_format: plain` means the prompt is sent as-is with no chat template applied, so the declared 256 prompt tokens are what reaches the engine and no template overhead has to be accounted for.
purpose: An 8B long-form writing assistant generating 4,000-token drafts from short prompts for 64 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 3885d340a4779c54662b10892555ae6928b3a090 (`git describe --tags` =
#   v0.20.1rc0-53-g3885d340a4779). It is a COMMIT on main and not a release, so it is named by
#   `configs/env.yaml: venv`. Interpreter, wheel and hardware live in that same file and are
#   NOT portable.
#
# SEMANTICS: one saturated single-GPU chat server at a short-prompt / very-long-generation shape,
# serving traffic that asks for repetition control. Nothing here is tuned; there is no
# tunable.yaml and no tuned.yaml.
#
# Every line below is either
#   (a) the value this engine resolves to for this model on this card, WRITTEN DOWN so the
#       in-process launcher cannot silently resolve a different one, or
#   (b) a declared choice, marked CHOSEN and listed in setupcard.md `chose_freely`.
#
# Every value below is ours and argued; none of it is quoted from anywhere.

# --- CHOSEN. A dense 8B instruct-capable checkpoint is the ordinary single-GPU serving scale at
# this engine's vintage, and Qwen3-8B is its ordinary representative here: ungated, complete in
# the local cache (5 shards, 16.38 GB), and known to this engine's model registry.
# Shape read off the cached config.json: Qwen3ForCausalLM, 36 layers, 32 query heads,
# 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, intermediate 12288, vocab 151936, bf16,
# max_position_embeddings 40960. 8.19B params = 16.38 GB = 15.26 GiB of weights.
# KV per token = 2 * 36 * 8 * 128 * 2 B = 147 456 B = 144 KiB.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B

# --- One card holds the weights and the working set; nothing in this setup needs a second.
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# --- The checkpoint's own dtype, pinned so a future default cannot drift it.
dtype: bfloat16

# --- PINNED, AND LOAD-BEARING. The ceiling on how many requests one decode step may hold. This
# item is declared at a SATURATED operating point: the 64 concurrent streams in scenario.json are
# meant to sit in ONE step, not partly queued behind this ceiling, so the two numbers are
# deliberately equal.
# It is also NOT the value an unpinned run would get. The per-usage-context default table in
# engine/arg_utils.py is consulted only for UsageContext.LLM_CLASS and OPENAI_API_SERVER; the
# engine is built in-process under ENGINE_CONTEXT, which is in neither branch, so an unpinned
# run falls through to SchedulerConfig.DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_SEQS = 128. 64 is therefore a
# CHOICE and not a default written down.
max-num-seqs: 64

# --- PINNED, AND NOT A DEFAULT. Same fall-through as above. 8192 is taken so that admitting new
# prompts is never the binding constraint of a workload that is decode-dominated by construction:
# a wave of 64 prompts at 256 tokens is 16 384 wire tokens, cleared in a couple of steps and then
# never contested again for the remaining 4095 decode steps. CHOSEN.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# --- CHOSEN. The longest request is 256 prompt + 4096 output = 4352 tokens. 4608 clears it with
# room and keeps the block tables far below the checkpoint's own 40960 window. Pinned rather than
# left at the checkpoint value because SchedulerConfig derives its token budget from
# max_model_len when the budget is unset, and leaving both unset makes one unpinned number depend
# on another.
max-model-len: 4608

# --- CHOSEN, AND SIZED. 0.90 * 79.6 GiB = 71.6 GiB, less 15.26 GiB of weights and roughly 5 GiB
# of activations, cudagraph pools and non-torch allocations, leaves on the order of 50 GiB of KV
# = ~364k tokens at 144 KiB/token. The steady state needs 64 streams * 4352 tokens = 278 528
# tokens = 38.2 GiB, so ALL 64 declared streams stay resident to the last token and the engine
# never preempts or recomputes. That headroom is the point: a run that preempts is not running
# this setup. If a future change to the shape eats it, LOWER THE OUTPUT LENGTH rather than
# raising this line.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# --- CHOSEN, AND LOAD-BEARING. This engine turns prefix caching ON by default
# (CacheConfig.enable_prefix_caching = True). It is forced OFF here so every request does its own
# prefill regardless of how many synthetic prompts happen to share a prefix. Nothing real is
# lost: the item is decode-dominated and the prompts carry no reusable context.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# --- THE DEFAULT, WRITTEN DOWN. `async_scheduling` is a tri-state that defaults to None and is
# then resolved in config/vllm.py: for a plain generation model with no speculative config and a
# supporting executor it resolves to True. It is pinned because it is a resolved default rather
# than a literal one -- its value depends on other config -- and because it changes the shape of
# the per-step bookkeeping the engine does. Stating it beats letting a build resolve it.
async-scheduling: true

# --- DELIBERATELY ABSENT, each an explicit decision:
#   quantization / kv-cache-dtype  -- the checkpoint is bf16 and nothing here quantises it.
#   enforce-eager                  -- absent, i.e. compilation and cudagraphs as this engine
#                                     ships them.
#   block-size                     -- left to the platform, which picks 16 on CUDA.
#   speculative / structured outputs / LoRA -- not part of this setup.
#   scheduling-policy              -- the fcfs default; the item does not contest scheduling.
#   enable-chunked-prefill         -- on by default at this commit; this setup never contests it,
#                                     since a 256-token prompt never exceeds the token budget.
#   more GPUs                      -- an 8B model at TP1 is the topology this item declares.
